summary:
本作の主人公。现代世界から相対未来の30世纪へ、戦舰のプレイヤーとしてスカウトとされた最初の女子高生。成绩优秀、スポーツ万能（アニメ版では运动部からたびたび助っ人に借り出され、みよね椎のコミック版ではバスケットボールの授业でその身长にもかかわらずダンクシュートを决めた）と、本人曰く、忙しい学校生活を送っている。また料理、裁缝など様々な分野に长けている他、演剧でもプロ颜负けの演技力を発挥し、学园祭ではシェークスピアの「お気に召すまま」のロザリンド役を见事に演じていた。唯一の欠点は欧米的な自己主张が强すぎる性格で、学校の教师からは厄介者扱いされている。原作においてアメリカで暮らしている祖母に、「その性格から日本社会に溶け込めないだろうから、大学、就职はアメリカに戻って来い」と言われていた。一方で同级生たちの间、取り分け女子生徒からは学年を问わず圧倒的な人気を夸っており、バレンタインデーの时には大量のチョコレートが赠られてくる（同性爱者の女生徒から赠られたチョコには、かなりいかがわしい内容の手纸が添付されていた）。
地元では名の通ったゲーマーでもあり、シューティングゲームで培った反射神経を駆使した操舰术で多くの舰を撃沈。途中からの参戦、特殊なミッションに駆り出されることが多かったために年间撃坠王には届かなかったものの、瞬く间にTERRAのエースパイロットとなった。
切れ长の眼（绿がかった色とされる）から猫のようなイメージをもたれることがあり、自身も猫を饲っているが彼女自身「猫」呼ばわりすることを毛嫌いしている。
ベルギー系アメリカ移民のクォーターで小学生までアメリカで暮らしていた帰国子女。日本の戸籍上は山本洋子であるが、フルネームは Yohko Dolores Asami Darlton Yamamoto（ヨーコ・ドロレス・アサミ・ダールトン・ヤマモト）となり、アメリカ时代「ヨーコ」という名前を呼びづらかったそちらの亲类や友人によって「ドロレス」(Dolores)というミドル・ネームで呼ばれていた。帰国后はそのことをひた隠しにしていたが理由は「ドロレス」の変形爱称に「ロリータ」が存在するため。
プロ野球「読売ジャイアンツ」のファンである。ゲームフリークではあるが真性のシューターであるためRPG、とりわけ「京都の花札屋」（任天堂を指す隠语）の制品を激しく嫌悪しており、同级生が学校に持ってきた新品のゲームソフトを校舎の2阶の窓から校庭に投げ舍てた事もある。RPG嫌いの原因は不明だが、漫画版では「めんどくさいから」という理由で迷路型要塞の通路を一直线にぶち破ってきていることから、头を使う类のゲームが苦手な模様。ゲームフリークとしては「北绫瀬の最终兵器」「ポリゴンの女王」などの通り名で呼ばれ、「京都を嫌わせれば羽田にも负けない」（それぞれ任天堂とセガを指す隠语）と言われる。
メオ・トロルのフーリガーとローソンの2人を憎からず思っているようだが积极的な行动に出ることは少なく、それが红叶の気を揉ませている一因にもなっている。一方でルージュがフーリガーに恋心を持っている事には気付いており、自分がフーリガーとダンスを踊った事をルージュにバラしてしまった时は彼女の怒りを恐れて狼狈するなど、他人の恋爱感情には敏感な部分がある。
3月6日生まれ、16歳。身长156cm。血液型AB型。嫌いな食べ物は纳豆、のり、生卵（ただし、テレビアニメの6话では自分で握ったおにぎりにのりが巻いてあった）。

魔人ザビエルの使徒。人间体の姿は颜デカブサイク男。先端に白骨の手が付いた杖を握っておりどもった话し方をする。本当の姿である玄武は岩石に覆われた象で、长い鼻の先に亀の头部が生えた巨大な怪物。 単独での戦闘力は他の使徒よりも低いが魔法に长けており、体力を全快させる最上位のヒーリングを习得している他、强力な结界や魔法Lv3级の魔法である异次元空间を作成することも可能だが、莫大な力を要する术を使う场合は暂くへばって动けなくなってしまう*1。魔法Lvの判定に困る手合いである。

LP5年、魔人ザビエルが复活すると、小早川ちぬの身体を割って复活。禁妖怪魂缚りの复活、黒姫の监视、岛津军の指挥、と、魔军の参谋として活跃する。 劣势になると脆弱な人间では頼りないからと魔物将军イスン、ベプチョ、ウィスピンの三名を魔物界から呼び寄せ、占领している各领に配置することで守りを固める。

最期は、织田军に南アフリカを制圧され、黒姫や魂缚りとエッチせんとするランスに挑み、本気を见せるも败れて死亡。

変身する际に自身の本当の名は玄武だと名乗っているため戯骸のように别名ではない。

Kokoro Momoiro was a victim of severe merciless bullying at her last school, and has resolved to never be a victim again. Upon arriving at Akademi, she immediately sought out the "bullies" of the school and desperately tried to get into their good graces for the purpose of making them see her as an ally, and not as a potential target. The firsthand knowledge of what it feels like to be bullied is still fresh in her mind, and she has absolutely no desire to abuse others, but she does it anyway...because she knows that she has to keep up the facade of being a bully in order to avoid being targeted by Musume and her friends. She has become what she hates, which has caused her to loathe herself deeply, but she would still rather hate herself than return to being harmed by others.

Perhaps one of the wisest decisions that Saisho Saikou ever made was to hide the majority of his personal beliefs and political stances from the public; most people would have been shocked or even outraged at some of his beliefs. For example, he was firmly convinced that the human race should proactively improve the quality of its population by excluding certain "inferior" genetic groups from reproduction, and promoting reproduction among other genetic groups judged to be "superior"...the textbook definition of eugenics. However, he knew that advocating for something so controversial would annihilate his public image, so he kept this belief - along with many others - a closely-guarded secret.

After going through great efforts to ensure that his offspring were as genetically "perfect" as possible, he was determined to prevent his children from ruining the gene pool that he had carefully cultivated. To this end, he insisted on selecting the woman that his son would marry. The process was identical to the one that he used to choose his first secretary, except now he was also carefully screening applicants for hereditary diseases, "undesirable" genes, and so on. The number of women who wished to marry into the Saikou family was very high, but the number of valid candidates was extremely low. Eventually, however, Saishou did find a woman who fulfilled his extremely specific criteria.

This woman, once an extremely ambitious and driven entrepreneur, was the CEO of the only tech company that stood even the slightest chance of competing against Saikou Corp. However, after it became clear that her business would never be able to outperform such Saisho's corporation, she made the difficult decision to liquidate her company. However, this was not an admission of defeat; it was the beginning of the next stage in her personal mission to "defeat" Saikou Corp. In her mind, becoming a permanent part of the Saikou family's legacy was the closest she would ever get to "winning" against them, so she applied for an arranged marriage with the founder's son.

The woman's credentials and genetics were perfect - but, before Saishou would allow this woman to become a part of the Saikou bloodline, he insisted on hiring her as his secretary, so that he could judge her competence firsthand. After he was firmly convinced that this woman was worthy of bearing his grandchildren, he allowed - or, rather, commanded - his son to marry her. By her logic, this made her "victorious" in her competition with Saikou Corp, and she relishes her status as the family's matriarch.

Aside from the fact that she has given birth to two healthy children and that she is always seen decorating her husband's arm at high-class events for social elites, there is little else that the public knows about her personal life after marrying into the Saikou family.

oze Shiuba - real name José Silva - is the treasurer of the student council in 1989.

Joze demonstrated a prodigious understanding of mathematics from a young age, earning him the nickname "A Calculadora Humana" - the Human Calculator - from his classmates. His family and peers encouraged him to attend the Olimpíada Brasileira de Matemática - the Brazilian Mathematical Olympiad - where he achieved a record number of gold medals. After this, he attended the 1988 International Mathematical Olympiad, where he scored a perfect 42/42 points, single-handedly turning Brazil into the winning country of that year's competition.

The Olympiad was held in Australia that year, and the experience of traveling to another country awakened something in Joze - an overwhelming desire to travel to as many countries as possible, and see as much of the world as he possibly could. Around this point in time, numerous academies and universities began to offer him scholarships; they viewed him as the type of rare, world-changing genius who only appears once or twice a century, and they were all very eager to welcome him into their facilities and see what kind of breakthroughs he could accomplish.

One of those invitations stood out to him - a scholarship offer from the world-famous Akademi Academy. Joze had been enamored with Japanese culture and aesthetics for as long as he could remember, and had even been studying the Japanese language in his spare time. So, out of all the options available to him, he chose to attend Akademi. He immediately intensified his study of the Japanese language, determined to arrive at Akademi with enough knowledge of Japanese to excel academically.

Upon arriving at Akademi, Joze was greeted by Reiichi Tanaami, who offered to grant him a tour of the school. When the two of them arrived in the student council room, Joze saw a stack of budget spreadsheets, and couldn't resist the urge to peek at them. Within seconds, he spotted errors and discrepancies that had slipped past the other members of the student council, and pointed them out to Reiichi. Reiichi instantly recognized the potential for Joze to become a valuable asset for the student council, and immediately offered him a position as the council's treasurer. Joze accepted.

Joze quickly became a popular topic of discussion among the female students of Akademi; some of them were impressed by his genius mind, others thought he was charming and thoughtful, and there were also some who perceived him as mysterious and "exotic" merely for being foreign-born. Despite being the subject of many whispered hallway conversations and stolen glances in class, Joze seemed completely unaware of the attention, too focused on his duties and studies to notice the effect that he had on the school's female population.

Although he succeeded in gaining enough mastery of the Japanese language to fully comprehend everything that his teachers said during class, he often became nervous and flustered the moment he had to converse in Japanese, and would often stutter and stumble his way through sentences with a mixture of Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, and even some random English. Although this embarrassed him immensely, most of his peers just thought it was really cute and endearing. He received a small amount of light teasing for his linguistic mistakes, but, overall, everyone at Akademi was quite accepting towards him.

After graduating from Akademi, Joze continued to travel the world, alternating back and forth between visiting his family in Brazil, traveling to various countries as a tourist, and teaching mathematics at prestigious universities worldwide. As time passed, Japan quickly became just one of many countries that Joze had stepped foot in during his travels. Although he didn't remain in direct contact with most of his old acquaintances from Akademi, he did find time to attend the funeral of his former colleague, Daisaku.

summary: パルミア教の异端审问官。又の名を《鬼谋》のミシェラン。

Hanzo was born in 1919 in Kyoto, Japan.

His father was a respected physician, and his mother was a teacher. His parents strongly believed that a man's contributions to the world were entirely dependent on the values he developed as a child, and so, starting from a young age, they strived to instill in him compassion, discipline, and reverence for human life.

Hanzo grew up quiet, intelligent, and empathetic. He excelled in biology, and intended to become a doctor like his father. He witnessed the gradual rise of militarism in Japan's schools: patriotic slogans, military drills, and the glorification of a large Japanese empire that constantly expanded, stretching as far as possible.

Many of these things seemed to directly contradict the values that were taught to him from early childhood onward. Conquering other people seemed like the exact opposite of compassion. The nationalistic words of his teachers made him feel uneasy at best, and physically sick at worst - but, he understood that voicing dissent would result in punishment, and so he stayed silent.

At 16, he began volunteering at his father's clinic, where he treated sick children, and began developed strong medical ethics that matched his strong morals. Shortly after he turned 18, he was drafted into the Imperial Japanese Army, where his medical skills resulted in him being assigned as a combat medic.

Hanzo arrived in China in November of 1937, shortly after a city had fallen to Japanese forces. He stepped off the transport ship onto a dock thick with smoke and debris, the scent of burning timber and gunpowder hanging in the air. Buildings along the waterfront were blackened and shattered. Most civilians still in the city were only there because they were too elderly, injured, or sick to flee.

Everywhere he looked, Hanzo felt the weight of human suffering pressing against him. He had been told that "victory" was something glorious, but all he could see here were broken lives. As he watched an injured civilian limping along in pain, he realized with a sinking heart that he might be the only person who could help him - but "rendering aid to the enemy" would be treason.

He knew that tending to civilians would result in punishment, but his urge to heal was stronger than his fear of the penalties he might face. He slipped into a medical supply tent at the edge of the Japanese encampment and started grabbing supplies - bandages, antiseptic, etc. Every moment in that tent was a gamble; if anyone noticed what he was doing, consequences would be immediate and severe.

Under the cover of dusk, Hanzo slipped away from the camp, keeping low and moving silently. In one alley, he found the man he had seen earlier, his leg bleeding from a jagged wound. Hanzo knelt beside him, cleaned the cut, wrapped it carefully, and bandaged it as best he could with the stolen supplies. The man's eyes widened in disbelief, then softened with relief as Hanzo finished.

A few blocks away, he found an old woman and her grandson huddled in the remains of a half-collapsed shop. He gave them what he could spare - bandages, antiseptic - and pointed out on a map where they could find a foreign concession where missionaries and aid workers had set up a temporary refuge. They nodded mutely, too exhausted to speak, but Hanzo saw a flicker of hope in their eyes.

Hanzo returned to the Japanese encampment, exhausted but resolute. No one had noticed his theft. For the first time in his life, Hanzo realized the kind of soldier he would never be: one who followed orders blindly. He would not allow his uniform to be an excuse to trample upon the lives of other human beings.

As Hanzo quietly slipped back among his fellow soldiers, he was relieved to see that, apparently, no one had noticed his absence; the day had been long, the men weary, and their attention was focused on the march that lay ahead. He took a seat near a group of soldiers, trying to appear as tired and indifferent as everyone else.

An innocuous conversation began nearby. The soldiers spoke of the terrain they would cross, rivers that might need to be forded, hills and rice paddies to navigate, narrow roads that could slow their progress. Questions of practicality arose naturally: If supplies run low, can villages along the way serve as sources of food and water? Are there friendly or neutral towns where they might resupply?

As the discussion continued, the tone shifted. The men spoke with increasing excitement about what they would take from villages: not just food, but whatever valuables they could find. Gradually, their words grew darker. One man laughed as he discussed "disciplining" villagers who might resist. The conversation spiraled into talk of beatings, executions, and worse. Hanzo's stomach twisted.

Hanzo had expected war to be harsh, but not cruel; he had expected his fellow soldiers to be disciplined, not openly and proudly devoid of any humanity. The more his countrymen talked, the more Hanzo came to understand the scale of what was coming: villages along the road to their destination would not simply be occupied; they would be destroyed.

Hanzo's mind raced. What could he do? He was just one medic. And yet, the more he thought about it, the more he realized what options were available to him. He could warn villages before the army arrived. He could steal supplies to aid civilians or resistance fighters. He could sabotage the army's preparations, slow them down, and give people a chance to survive.

For the first time, a clear purpose crystallized in his mind: he would dedicate himself to saving lives wherever he could. Not every village could be reached, not every plan could be foiled - but even small acts of intervention would matter. Hanzo silently vowed to act wherever possible, every day of the march, to protect those who could not protect themselves.

Hanzo allowed himself to get a few hours of sleep, but rose before the dawn. While the other soldiers slept, he gathered some supplies and then left the encampment, heading towards the first village that the Japanese army would encounter on its march. The trek would be exhausting, but he was willing to endure the strain on his body if it meant he could save lives.

When Hanzo reached the first village along the planned marching route, the villagers stared at him with eyes wide with fear and suspicion. He knew that if he tried to speak, they would not understand him - or worse, panic at the sound of a Japanese accent. He knew that he would have to rely on body language and hand gestures to communicate his warning to them.

First, he took out a map that he had brought with him, and laid it out on the ground. Then, he pointed to the insignia on his uniform - the small Japanese flag stitched onto his sleeve - and then to the position of the Japanese encampment. Using his finger, he traced a line from the encampment toward the village, indicating the path of the advancing army.

Next, Hanzo mimed firing a rifle at the villagers. He waved his arms violently, doing whatever he could do communicate the idea of danger and violence. Finally, he waved his hands back and forth in sweeping gestures, moving toward the villagers and then away, repeating the motion until they understood what he was trying to tell them: Leave. Go. Escape.

The villagers began to speak amongst themselves. Hanzo listened carefully to their words. The word they said when they pointed to him. The word they said when they pointed in the direction of the approaching Japanese army. He pointed at the patch on his uniform, and repeated the word. The villagers seemed surprised, but nodded. He realized that this was the word for "Japanese."

It took some time, but he managed to confirm the words for "Japanese" "army" "kill" "village" and "evacuate." The villagers came to understand their dire situation, and began to move swiftly, gathering their children and belongings, heading for someplace safer, far away from the route that the Japanese army would be taking.

Hanzo breathed a massive sigh of relief; now that he had learned the essential vocabulary he would need for future warnings, each subsequent village would be easier to communicate with. He realized that, even without speaking the same language, he could convey life-saving information - and, in the process, gradually pick up the words that would allow him to speak more effectively.

However, his relief would be short-lived.

"What are you doing?"

Hanzo's blood went cold. His heart hammered as he spun around. A Japanese soldier stood there, rifle slung casually over one shoulder, cap pulled low, almost hiding his face. Hanzo swallowed hard. His first thought: "I will be executed." If word of what he had done reached the officers, there would be no trial; just a bullet. He scrambled to find the words that would get him out of this situation.

However, he quickly realized that lying would not save him. Instead, he steeled himself and spoke the truth. He knew that the Japanese army planned to commit countless atrocities in this country, and he refused to be complicit in any of it. But, just refusing to participate was not enough; he wanted to save as many lives as possible, even if it meant sabotaging his own countrymen.

The soldier calmly listened to Hanzo's emotional speech. He tilted his head, watching him with unreadable eyes. There was no anger on his face - in fact, there was no emotion at all. Only a clinical detachment, as though Hanzo were an insect in a glass jar. After what seemed like forever, the finally soldier spoke, his tone flat and uninflected.

"You're going to get killed if you keep doing this," he said, his voice calm, as if he was merely commenting on the weather. "...but...if you absolutely refuse to stop...I guess I'll help you. I'll...make things easier for you."

Hanzo blinked, stunned. "You...would do that?"

The soldier's eyes did not soften. There was no smile, no warmth - only an unnerving, calm gaze that seemed to cut straight through him. "Yes. I refuse to let you die."

Hanzo exhaled slowly, a wave of relief washing away the knot of fear in his chest. Against all odds, he had found an ally. Someone who, perhaps, shared his disgust with the path their countrymen had chosen. However, there were still a few things that he would need to know before he was completely comfortable working together with this person.

"What is your name?"

The soldier hesitated, as if he needed a moment to remember what his name was. "Private Sato."

"Why are you out here alone, so far ahead of the army? Were you planning to desert? To defect?"

The soldier looked away, as if searching for the truth somewhere. "Sure. Let's go with that."

Everything about this person felt off. Suspicious. Wrong. But, Hanzo didn't really have the luxury of being picky with his allies at this point in time. He chose to simply be thankful that, out of all the soldiers in the Japanese army, the one person who knew his secret was somebody who intended to help him instead of snitching on him.

And so, the rhythm of the next month was established. By day, Hanzo marched with his unit in the endless column of men snaking through the countryside. His boots struck the dirt in unison with thousands of others. The air was filled with shouted orders, the metallic clatter of rifles, and the weary silence of men conserving their strength.

But, in the pale gray of early morning, before his countrymen awoke, Hanzo slipped away. Sometimes with a limp, muttered excuse about checking equipment. Sometimes vanishing so quietly that no one noticed at all. In those stolen hours, he crossed fields and crept into villages that still slept under the illusion of safety.

With a map, a handful of Chinese words, and some universally understood body language, Hanzo was able to convince numerous Chinese villages to completely evacuate long before the Japanese army arrived, ensuring their survival. And, at each village, he learned just a few more valuable Chinese words, allowing him to communicate more effectively in the future; to carry each warning farther.

"Private Sato" aided Hanzo in whatever way he could. Sometimes, this was as simple as covering for him when he was absent. Other times, Sato provided valuable information, such as which villages were at greatest risk. He even provided distractions that would allow Hanzo to sneak out without being caught. His demeanor was still just as unsettling as ever, but he was an invaluable ally.

With time, Hanzo gradually grew bolder; when he was not saving lives, he was finding ways to slow the progress of the Japanese army. At first, his sabotage was small, almost invisible: he loosened straps so packs of ammunition would fall unnoticed into the mud. He loosened a wheel just enough that it would rattle off on the march. Nobody suspected him; "Accidents happen. It is what it is."

But, as the days turned into weeks, his courage hardened. He began slashing ropes in the dead of night, scattering ammunition into the fields, and pouring precious drinking water onto the ground where no one would notice until morning. Food shortages worsened, vehicles broke down at critical moments. His acts of resistance grew into blows that truly hindered the machinery of conquest.

Sato escalated with him. He guided Hanzo past watchful sentries with uncanny timing. He calmly offered to "take care of" soldiers who were growing suspicious - though Hanzo always refused, chilled by the blunt casualness in his tone. When Hanzo agonized over the danger, Sato only replied, "Like I told you...I don't intend to let you die."

One night, after nearly a month of his efforts, as Hanzo began to creep out of the Japanese encampment in the early hours of the morning, just as he had done so many times before...a rough hand grabbed his shoulder. He knew exactly what this meant. He slowly turned around, knowing exactly what he would see before he saw it: A group of soldiers, staring at him with narrowed eyes.

"I knew it."
"So, it was you, after all."
"I always thought there was something off about you."

The soldier closest to him raised a fist and struck him across the ribs, knocking the wind out of him. Another kicked him in the side, and he collapsed into the dirt, gasping for air. The savage beating he received over the next few minutes was not meant to kill him; it was meant to punish and humiliate the man who had made the past month of their lives much harder than it needed to be.

Finally, after they were satisfied with the amount of punishment they had dealt to him, they bound his hands behind his back with rope and roughly dragged him toward the center of the camp. A crowd of soldiers was gathered there, having heard that some of their comrades had finally figured out the identity of the traitor who had been sabotaging their operations over the past month.

Just as he had once mused to himself, there really would be no trial. A commanding officer barked orders, and a small group of soldiers assembled rifles for a swift execution. Hanzo's chest tightened with a mixture of pain and fear. He tried to comfort himself with thoughts of the lives that he had saved, but when staring down the barrels of a set of rifles, terror is inevitable.

He was forced to stand before a hastily dug trench, bruised and bloodied, rifles aimed at him. The air was cold and still. The first pale light of dawn was just beginning to creep over the horizon. Hanzo closed his eyes tightly, and attempted to picture the faces of the people he had helped in a desperate attempt to convince himself that his death was a small price to pay for their safety.

Then,

BOOOOOOOOOOM!!!!!!!!!!

A sudden, deafening explosion ripped through the camp, and smoke billowed in every direction, obscuring the view of the firing squad. Hanzo lost his balance and dropped to the ground, ears ringing, heart hammering. Then, through the chaos, he heard something growing louder and louder - the roar of an engine.

A military transport truck drove at full-speed towards Hanzo, cutting through the smoke and confusion, then skidded to a stop beside him. A person whose silhouette he vaguely recognized exited the truck, yanked him to his feet, shoved him into the vehicle, slammed the door shut, then climbed back into the driver's seat.

"...Sato?"

As always, the stone-faced soldier's hands were steady, expression calm despite the chaos he had just created. He slammed the gas pedal to the floor, tearing through the encampment at top speed. Soldiers shouted at them and raised their weapons, but the thick smoke and disorientation bought them precious seconds. They tore down a dirt road away from the camp.

Once they were a safe distance away, Sato took the truck off-road, drove deep into a forest, came to a stop in a location where the truck would be hidden by thick brush, and turned the engine off. He removed the rope around Hanzo's wrists, freeing him and allowing him to finally sit up in his seat and catch his breath.

Hanzo turned to look at Sato, the man who had just risked his life to save him - a man who would now be branded a traitor and hunted by the Japanese military. "Sato...why?" he asked, voice hoarse, still in pain from the beating earlier. "Why would you do so much for me? Why would you throw away everything for me?"

Sato stared directly forward for a few moments, then removed his military cap. For once, Hanzo actually got a clear look at Sato's face. His features were calm, resolute...and...feminine. Not only that, but his features were...familiar. Wait. Hanzo knew that face. He had seen that face before. Back in Japan. He knew this man. No...

...he knew this woman.

"Why, you ask? It's because I love you."

Hanzo's mouth dropped open as he tried to absorb the revelation that was unfolding in front of him. Sato was a woman - and not just any woman; this was a classmate of his. They had gone to the same school together. This woman, who hadn't even graduated high school yet, who just rescued him from certain death, was...

"...Arisa Aishi, is that you?"

For the first time, her expression changed. "You said my name..." She blushed - like a shy, embarrassed schoolgirl receiving a compliment from her crush - and turned away, burying her face in her hands. It was as though she had transformed into a different person altogether. Hanzo had a thousand questions, but only enough breath to ask the most obvious one:

"...how? Women aren't allowed in the army."

"I...I wanted to be near you. So, when you were conscripted, I dropped out of school. I started working in a factory next to the camp where you had basic training. Just to watch you. To make sure that you were alright."

Hanzo was so touched by these words that his hand flew to his chest, right over his heart. "Arisa, that's..." It didn't occur to him that this could be the behavior of a psychotic, obsessive stalker. He just thought that it was heartwarming. "...that's so sweet."

"I couldn't just sit around in Kyoto, pretending life was normal, knowing that you were about to go to war, out of my sight, out of my reach. One night, I saw a boy from your unit slip out of the camp at night. He was deserting. He stripped off his uniform, left it in the dirt, ran off into the night, and never came back. The next morning, he would've been reported missing. But...his uniform was just lying there, so...I took it. His name. His place in your unit. His entire identity."

"And *nobody* noticed?" Hanzo was in disbelief. "What about the medical exam we all had to go through?"

"The boy had already passed that exam. That's why it worked. The records said he was fit, so when I took his place, all I had to do was meet the bare minimum, and nobody thought to question it. Kept my hair short, my voice low, my head down, and I was just another face in the crowd of boys."

"...and then, you followed me all the way here?"

Arisa smiled faintly. "Where else would I go? Your side is where I belong."

It would take Hanzo time to process everything that had just transpired - getting caught, almost being executed, being saved by "Sato," the big reveal that Sato was actually an old female classmate, and the even bigger reveal that she loved him enough to impersonate a male, join the army, and travel to China...but in the meantime, he couldn't just sit in that truck. He had to act.

Hanzo knew that the Japanese army would not give up searching for him, and that their hiding spot would eventually be discovered. He knew that they had to get as far away from the Japanese army as possible. He exited the truck, and quickly realized that he could barely walk - the savage beating he had gotten from his countrymen had nearly crippled him. But Arisa was there for him to lean on.

After carefully studying a map of the surrounding area, Hanzo and Arisa determined the optimal place to hide out - a Chinese village that was far away from the Japanese army's path. It was possible that some of those people in that village would be people who Hanzo had encountered in the past, when warning villages to evacuate and take refuge elsewhere. Hanzo might be recognized as an ally.

Although every step of the journey was painful - not just figuratively, but literally, because Hanzo was still recovering from that beating - they eventually made it to the Chinese village. Just as they had hoped, Hanzo saw familiar faces there. Apparently, he had become something of a local folk hero, and the villagers were happy to repay his kindness towards them by helping him recuperate.

Hanzo spent several weeks regaining his strength from the beating he had endured after being identified as a saboteur. During this time, he wrestled with an obvious question: "What do we do now?" Once able to walk and fight again, what options were open to him? He still abhorred the Japanese military and still wished to actively aid the Chinese, but had no long-term plan of action.

Hanzo and Arisa initially planned to simply offer labor and protection to villages on the fringes of occupied territory, but a chance encounter soon brought them into contact with a cell of the Chinese Communist Eighth Route Army. The cell, composed of peasant fighters, student revolutionaries, and a few former Japanese soldiers, saw value in Hanzo and Arisa, who were welcomed into the cell.

The years that followed were not marked by constant combat, but by the steady rhythm of guerrilla life. Hanzo and Arisa became specialists in tasks that played to their unique skills. Hanzo, with his fluency in Japanese military procedures, provided intelligence on patrol routes, supply convoys, and garrison habits.

Arisa, able to pass more easily as an ordinary villager, carried messages, scouted terrain, and gathered supplies. Together, they participated in carefully chosen acts of sabotage: cutting rail lines, derailing Japanese trains, or ambushing supply caravans when the risk was low and the rewards high.

The cell survived by blending into the countryside. Months might pass with little fighting, filled instead with farming, repairing tools, drilling recruits, and moving between safe houses. When Japanese reprisals threatened a village, Hanzo and Arisa joined the fighters in dispersing to the hills, hiding in caves or forests until it was safe to return.

By the time the war reached its conclusion in 1945, Hanzo and Arisa had spent nearly six years living among the guerrillas. They had fought only when necessary, but their intelligence work and selective sabotage operations had saved countless lives and made them respected figures within the resistance.

With the war over, Hanzo faced a profound crossroads. Six years of life as a guerrilla fighter had taken its toll on him, and he yearned to return to civilian life...however, that there was one last thing he had to do before he could return to Japan: make sure that anyone who had committed atrocities during the war was punished for their actions.

Hanzo insisted on providing testimony to Allied and Chinese authorities. His motivations were clear: to ensure that individual soldiers, officers, and commanders who had ordered or carried out atrocities in occupied China were not allowed to escape justice. Hanzo's credibility as a Japanese defector - one who had not only deserted but actively resisted - made him a rare and valuable witness. Arisa, though less directly tied to military records, corroborated accounts of massacres, forced labor, and other crimes she had seen or heard of during her time with the guerrillas.

They were summoned to Nanjing, where the International Military Tribunal for the Far East and subsidiary Chinese war crimes courts sought testimony from those who had firsthand knowledge of Japanese misconduct in China. Hanzo described incidents ranging from the burning of villages suspected of harboring guerrillas, to the routine execution of civilians accused of aiding resistance fighters. His ability to identify specific officers, units, and procedures was especially valuable. Arisa, drawing on her experiences in the countryside, spoke of reprisals, starvation, and the destruction of civilian livelihoods.

The couple's testimony, though painful to recount, was incorporated into the larger body of evidence used to prosecute Japanese officers in both international and domestic Chinese trials. Some of the men Hanzo named were sentenced to prison, or were outright executed; they would never be allowed to disappear into postwar chaos and hide in the shadows, avoiding responsibility forever.

Only after this duty was fulfilled did Hanzo and Arisa quietly return to Japan. They recognized that their role as defectors would earn them the hatred of their fellow countrymen, so they carefully constructed a cover story for themselves to hide the truth of what they had really been doing over the past 6 years.

By blending back into ordinary society, and by carefully concealing the years they had spent abroad, they were able to live the rest of their lives as anonymous citizens in the shadows of postwar Japan. However, what Hanzo had seen during the war left him with a permanent distaste for his home country. No matter how many years passed, he was never able to forgive Japan.

Hanzo made sure that his children and grandchildren were well aware of Japan's actions during WW2, and he cautioned them to never be blindly patriotic to their home country. This "generational dislike for Japan" eventually manifested in a desire to leave Japan altogether, and Hanzo's descendants would eventually move out of Japan and live in America.

闘神としては比较的小柄な纯金制の身体を持ち、格闘机能に特化した女性型の闘神で、别名「黄金の女神」。
圣魔教団五人众の1人であるが、闘神の戦闘スタイルはガチガチの格闘タイプ。
魔人戦争において、当时No.1の荒くれ者であった魔人ノスと70日にも及ぶ殴り合いをした事で后世に伝えられる。

闘神Θの真髄は异常とも言える回避能力にあり、魔人ノスの拳を见てから躱せるほどであった。
単纯ながら究极の対処法であり、70日间の戦闘において、たった一撃掠めたのみだったと言う。
一方、闘神Θの攻撃は全てノスに命中するも、地竜の膨张硬化特性により尽く受け切られる。
殴って躱す、これを缲り返すこと70日、闘神Θは无伤であったが闘神都市侧のコアが陥落。
机能停止した闘神Θはノスの拳を受け破壊される结末となった。
ただ、自らの力で闘神Θを打ち倒すことの出来なかったノスは怒り狂い、その矛先は他の闘神へ。

闘神自体が魔人と戦う为に造られたとは言え、基本的には都市中央から指示を出すのが本来の役目。
彼女が后世まで语り継がれているのは、他の闘神とは违う事をしたからこそ。

ノスとの闘いで名を上げた「黄金の女神」は、吟游诗人达の间で最も歌われている闘神である。
このエピソードにより、世间では闘神と言えばシータ、魔人と言えばノスという程に强い认知度を持つ。

かつて収监された少女が魔女になってし まった『魔女のなれはて」。国が开発した、魔女を制御す装置头に何かが刺さつ ていもの)によって洗脳されている。
洗脳済みの个体は牢屋敷のために働て おり、ゴクチョや[mask]メルル[/mask]の命令で动いている。牢屋敷の看守スタッフにする『魔女のなれはて』は[mask]メルル[/mask]にー任されており、比较的大人く従顺だった少が看守と して働かされている。键の管理や牢屋敷 の保全、処刑を担当したり、脱狱者がいないか见回ったている。特にイレュラな事态がなければ、毎日同じスク缲り返てい。
[mask]作中の看守はの姉。[/mask]黒衣と仮面で多くは隠れているが、2メ一トル以上の大きさで、手足の造形が明らかに人间とは违うとわかる。

原罪：支配された魔女のなれはて

魔法：
なれはてになるとそれまで所持していた魔法は失われ る、抜け壳のようなもの。但し魔女として死なない体を 持っており、クリーチャー化したことで常轨を逸した身体 能力を持つ（身体能力の高いシェリーでも一时的に抵 抗する程度しかできない)。普段の动きは缓慢。

Adopted by the Malto family, Thrash Malto is a Terran, one of the first of a new generation of Transformers born on Earth. Closest to Mo, the two of them are fast friends, goofing off and playing games together. Thrash would do anything for her, and even his motorcycle-and-sidecar alternate mode was inspired by her old bike. While his connection is strongest with Mo, the siblings' emotions are all connected through the mysterious cyber-sleeves.

summary:
你说我的过去吗？就和那些故事书里的海盗一样——在海上当恶霸，欺负被我盯上的家伙，过着每天都不一样的生活~可惜运气不好，碰上了硬茬，快乐的日子就只能被迫结束咯。
角色设定
荒海を駆けた舰船「テンペスタ」の一人。掟约（じょうやく）のテンペスタ。
畅気で自由奔放、日々の生活を満吃するタチだが、しばしば时代错误でドライな発言をして仲间たちを惊かせることも…？

和镇海一样，我是从属于东煌的水上飞机母舰。可惜备好的兵刃还未出鞘，一切便成了白费功夫……哎呀，不说这些让人提不起劲的事了。你不是答应了我，带我一起做些高兴的事吗？
角色设定
东煌所属の軽空母、古式ゆかしい深闺（しんけい）の令嬢…
などではなく、おしとやかながらもワクワクドキドキを求めるちょっとやんちゃな东煌少女。
ノリが良くても、辛い料理だけはどうしても苦手。

ヤシロの友达の勇者。笑颜の里に何を考えているのか分からない底知れなさがある。
ヒトの断末魔の悲鸣を录音するのが趣味。

かつてベゼルアイが产んだレア女の子モンスター。名前の通り、泥で出来た体を持つ。歌うように意味不明な言叶で喋り、その内容はアムぐらいしか理解が出来ない。一见キチガイのようだが、行动そのものは案外まともである。
モドカタを人质とされ、シャングリラ?の分身体ケイブリスの警护にあたっていたが、ランス达に败北。その责を取らされ、ベスドク山の地下水路の警备に回される。汚水により肉体も头脳もボロボロの状态で再びランス达に遭遇し、さすがに境遇を哀れんだランスに仲间になるよう诱いをかけられるも、爱しい夫のためそれを拒否して戦いを挑む。再败北后は既にモドカタがケイブリスに杀害されていたことすら知ることなく、无惨に消灭していった。

kana: さいおんじ クレア
summary:
43歳
クリスの母亲で、主人公のママ同様に未亡人。
イギリス人と日本人のハ一フで、金髪に爆乳が际立つ美魔女。
亡くなった旦那の会社と遗产を引き継いでおり、
その映像関系の小さな会社の女社长。
だがその隠れた才能により事业の方は顺调で、
豪华な豪邸に高级スポ一ッカ一を何台も所有するス一パ一セレブ。
仕事によるストレスによって性欲の方も溜まりに溜まっており、
その性欲は性豪と呼ばれるほど。
その豊満な肉体を持て余すように、セックスの方も肉食系で
彼女の方からガンガン攻めるタイプ。

穂群原学园2年A组に所属する谜の森ガール。その正体は黒魔术を得意とし、「いずれ圣杯戦争に强制的に参加せねばならない」という颈木から解放されたフリーダムな绫香。亲が存命、姉との仲も良好だが、目の前で优秀な姉が駄目人间化していくのを目撃。そして龙脉直上での修行が彼女に「自信が持でる最低限ライン」までの腕前修得を成功させ、「この家は私がしっかりしないと…!!」という精神変化も引き起こし、プロトタイプ绫香のような内向性・自信のなさ・自虐的性格は発生しなかった。
魔女の釜が设置されている薄暗い地下室で魔术书を読みまくったせいで纯粋に视力が低いため、眼镜を外して性格スイッチ…といった技能もない。パーフェクトナチュラル眼镜ッ娘。
2年の夏にロンドンへ赴き「时计搭」に体験入学をした。その际に「サジョウ」の名に兴味を示した时计塔のカリスマとの縁が生まれ、ほんの一时であるが师事を受け、「生け贽用の动物を杀すことに抵抗あるなら植物メインでやっていく方向もある」という助言を授かったことが天启というか致命的というかこの世界线における绫香に决定的な何かを方向づけてしまったらしい。
当然植物だけの黒魔术などどう転んでも破绽しかないわけでトラップ的な意味の助言であり、将来的には培った黒魔术の才と本来の才である元素変换（フォーマルクラフト)をハイブリッドした何かに落とし込むというのがカリスマの目论见だったのだが……………。

summary:
■说明

デストロンの大干部のひとり、ヨロイ元帅の本当の姿。ザリガニの特性を持つ。

无数のトゲを备えた坚牢な甲罗で全身を覆っており、左腕の先端はハサミ型になっている。口から発火性の泡を放射したり、地中を自由に移动する能力を备えている。

また、背中には锐い脚を备えた巨大な蟹のような甲罗を背负っており、それを取り外して足で踏み砕き、破片を相手に投げつけるという「甲罗くずし」という奥の手がある。

强大な破壊力を持つ兵器「プルトンロケット」の制造中に、作戦を知った者に対してザリガーナの姿となり、人知れず始末していた。

基地内に潜入した结城丈二ことライダーマンの前でもザリガーナの姿を披露し戦闘。続けて现れた仮面ライダーV3とも戦いを缲り広げるが、その间に自らを犠牲にしたライダーマンによって、プルトンロケットは破壊されてしまった。

次なる作戦として、首领の命令により「D作戦」を敢行。再生された怪人たちを率いて大规模な破壊活动を行うと同时に「少年仮面ライダー队」の関系者を袭撃し、队员たちや珠纯子を诱拐した。

その后、処刑场に乱入してきたV3を迎え撃ち、最初はヨロイ元帅の姿で戦っていたが、途中でザリガーナに変化。だが、背中の甲罗に备わる脚を次々ともぎ取られために焦って距离を置くと、奥の手となる甲罗くずしを仕挂ける。だが投げつけた破片はV3に难なくよけられてしまい、続けてまるで结城丈二への仕打ちを返されたが如く、左腕のハサミを破壊されてしまう。もはや反撃する术もなく、トドメとばかりに放たれた「V3フル回転キック」を受けて倒れると、ヨロイ元帅の姿へと戻ってしまった。

这々の体でアジトへと逃げ帰り首领に助けを求めたが、役立たずの烙印を押された挙げ句に怒りの一撃を受けて爆破、消灭する哀れな末路を辿った。



なお、第52话にも再生怪人として登场している。



身长：179.0cm

体重：87.0kg

特色/力など：左腕のハサミ、甲罗くずし、口から吐く発火性の泡、地中を移动



声：沢りつお（さわ・りつお）

盖亚的千万自我重合为一，在时光之茧中获得了前所未有的极致突破。灭战神决·盖亚斗气雄浑，力拔山岳，他是永恒的战神，带给正义以希望。

即使力量枯竭、粉身碎骨，盖亚也绝不会让自己的双拳向邪恶投降。只有战至最后一刻，方显战神本色。
绝魇魔女彻底解放自我，接受了咤克斯赐予的力量，强大的能量扩散而出，将雷伊和盖亚二人逼退数米。敌人虽然强大，但盖亚心中的强烈信念依然在熊熊燃烧。就在这时，盖亚似乎感受到了一些不一样的东西——他的眼前突然出现了无数个他自己。不，不止“眼前”……他的身边，那些“自己”的身边，更为遥远的地方，甚至是在其他的世界中，都浮现出了各式各样的盖亚身影。他们有的流露着圣光的气息，有的像是真正的帝王，有的穿戴着堡垒般的重甲，有的是充满豪气的游侠，而其中有的还只是一脸不屈的孩子……无数个不同世界、不同时期的盖亚纷纷走来，他们与盖亚站在了一起，一同握紧了绝不服输的拳头。这一瞬间，似乎有跨越时空的无数力量汇聚为奔流的波涛，填满了这个时光之茧，涌入了盖亚的身体。
不灭的信念产生的回响充满了无数的历史空间。战胜邪恶的渴望变为呼唤，招来了源源不断增长的力量。盖亚与无数个自己站在了一起，一种堪称奇迹的极致突破出现在了他的身上。他的感官变得更加敏锐，拳风变得更为凌厉，并且这种力量的增长持续不断，没有止境。
灭战神决·盖亚的双拳已经做好了应对咤克斯降临的准备，他将以无上的战神之姿，消灭黑暗，带来光明。

summary:
巾帼不让须眉，红颜更胜儿郎！麒麟之女决战天下，英姿飒爽女中豪杰！

岁月如一支利剑，带着急速的光芒勇往直前，又锋利无边。
蓦然回首，才知道已经过去了那么久了，而眼前的父亲，似乎也随着时间而增添了几分沧桑。
她的父亲是高贵强大的守护神兽，作为麒麟之女，再加上了极高的天赋，她的职责也本该如此。只是那时的波西利亚还太过的年幼，不明守护为何，亦毫无兴趣，桀骜不驯的性格令她毅然决然地离开了故乡，踏上了游历之旅。
起初她还很高兴，一路上用自己的强大的力量救死扶伤、匡扶正义，打退了多少的地痞无赖呢？可能她也不记得了吧。
逐渐地，这种重复且单一的事情让她感觉到些许厌烦，难道她的旅途就是这样的吗？日复一日的收拾这些的地痞流氓？可宇宙之大，恶棍何其之多，凭借着她的双手何以除的尽呢？
她究竟该怎样呢？她的道路又在哪里呢？
不得不说，陷入了深深的自我怀疑以及迷茫之中，是一件很可怕的事情，每天所做的一切都索然无味，恍若梦中梦，心间只有一片云雾缭绕。
直到那一天，她遇到了一位与她不相上下的对手，与之战斗的过程中，她体会到了一种难以想象的畅快之感，心中熄灭已久的斗志，恍若火焰般熊熊燃起，而她，也终于找到了自己的道路。
或许，这一身天赋注定用于与强者为战，站在前线面对真正的敌人，用双手耗尽自己全部的力量去除治邪恶，还这个世界一份和平，似乎才是她应该做的。

だから、心置きなく抱けばいい、注げば注ぐほど、彼女は深く悦ぶのだから。

求められ、受け入れる。それだけの関系。

故に、彼女は男を爱する娼妇である

辉装LEVEL 1：永劫操姫 （アイオン・コッペリア）


凌驾と同じ学年に属する优等生。
高名な政治家の娘という出自、端丽な容貌、优秀な成绩といった数々の天赋の要素と本人の才覚により、学园のマドンナとして憧れの视线を集めている。

しかし、家族を袭った悲剧により天涯孤独の身の上となってからは、他人には见せない一面を宿すようになっている。
そのためか人前では温厚な令嬢然として振る舞うが、敌と见なしたものを攻撃する时は彻底して容赦がない。
いわば里表を使い分ける仮面优等生。その秘密を一端とはいえ凌驾に知られてからは、彼を○く意识しはじめることに。

学帽・黒マントに学生服という、弊衣破帽を体现した出で立ちの青年。

また腰元にはサーベル拵えの军刀を佩用しており、明らかに只者ではない雰囲気を漂わせる。
その身なりは时代错误としか思えないが、信天岛の馆においては当世风にマッチしてしまっている。
彼は、ここ5年より向こうの记忆がないという重度の记忆丧失状态。
にも関わらず本人にそれを気に挂ける様子はなく、原因不明ながら究明しようともしていない。
その影响ゆえなのか、バンカラな格好とは里腹に穏やかな気性の持ち主。
そんな彼の职业は“探侦”。 奇抜な発想と豊かな想像力で培われた彼の推理は、余计なものに惑わされていないつもりでも、大きく的を外してしまうケースが目立つ。
だが、そのおかげで事件を解决してしまうことが多く、依頼人からの评判も良い。
その评価を受けるのは、本人にとっていささか不本意であるものの、解决して良かったと思う気持ちが○いため、その“迷”推理を省みたことは一度もない。
彼の用いる军刀は考え事をする际に役立つらしく、一振りするたびに头が冴え渡るというが真相は不明。
まだ见习いの身分だが、信天岛のとある谜を解明すべく招かれたという。
しかしその反面で、本人はそれ以外の目的意识も持っているようだが……？

summary:
リメイク版DQ6における、【スライムスカウト】で仲间になる【マリンスライム】。
仲间モンスターシステムがあるDQ5やDQ8を含めても、この手の贝壳スライムが仲间になるのは初めてである。
マリリンという名前は割とふさわしいとは言え、SFC版プレイヤーにとっては【リップス】の仲间モンスターの1匹目の名前という印象が强いだろう。
　
「ほっといてよ。アタシ、悪いマリンスライムなの」な决め台词。また、「キュルルン」も口癖となっている。
しかし実际に悪いわけではなく、亲友の【ベホマン】に対する気耻ずかしさから世界中を逃げ回っており、そんな意気地のない自分に対する自戒の念が「悪いマリンスライムなの」である。何というツンデレスライム。
最初に出会えるのは何とゲーム开始直后であり、上ライフコッドの井戸にいる。
以降、ベホマンから逃げる形で下レイドックの港など、上下の世界を超えてあちこちを巡り、最后は世界の果て、海底の宿屋に落ち着く。
ここにベホマンを连れて行くことで、逃げてばかりだった自分を反省し、仲间になる。
